name: Pend Oreille County

How Pend Oreille County, Washington, Conducts Tax Sales – A Complete Guide

Pend Oreille County, Washington, holds tax sales to recover unpaid property taxes. If property owners fail to pay taxes for three years, the county starts foreclosure proceedings and auctions off the property. These sales happen through public auctions, giving buyers a chance to purchase properties at competitive prices. To stay updated, check the Auction Calendar for scheduled sales.

How the Auction Works

The Pend Oreille County Treasurer’s Office oversees tax foreclosure auctions. The process begins when the Treasurer files a Certificate of Delinquency, listing all properties with unpaid taxes. Before the auction, the county:
  • Publishes a legal notice in the local newspaper and on the Treasurer’s website.
  • Notifies property owners and lienholders about the foreclosure.
  • Allows property owners to pay overdue taxes to avoid foreclosure.
If the owner does not pay by the deadline, the property goes to auction. Pend Oreille County typically conducts auctions online through Bid4Assets, allowing buyers to bid from anywhere.

Auction Rules and Requirements:

  • Registration – Buyers must register online before bidding.
  • Deposit Requirement – Some auctions require a refundable deposit to participate.
  • Minimum Bids – The starting bid includes unpaid taxes, interest, and foreclosure costs.
  • Highest Bid Wins – The property goes to the bidder who offers the most.

How to Prepare for the Auction

Pend Oreille County sells all properties as-is, so buyers must research before bidding.

Key Steps Before Bidding:

  1. Check the property list – Review parcel numbers, legal descriptions, and bid amounts.
  2. Confirm the property location – Use maps and records to verify access and boundaries.
  3. Investigate liens or claims – Some properties may have outstanding debts that buyers must handle.
  4. Understand property use rules – Some properties have zoning restrictions.
  5. Determine occupancy status – If occupied, buyers must follow legal eviction procedures.
  6. Check land access – Some properties lack road access and require further research.
  7. Review utility availability – Some parcels may not have water, electricity, or sewage connections.

Bidding Process

Pend Oreille County auctions follow an online bidding format. The bidding process works as follows:
  • Register before the auction – Sign up on the Bid4Assets auction platform.
  • Start bidding at the minimum price – The opening bid covers all outstanding county taxes and fees.
  • Increase bids as needed – Raise your offer until the auction closes.
  • Highest bid wins – The auction ends when no further bids are placed.
  • Automatic extensions – Some auctions extend closing times if bidders place bids near the end.

Payment and Deadlines

Winning bidders must pay in full by the county’s deadline. The county only accepts cash, cashier’s checks, and money orders. Personal checks and credit cards are not allowed.

Important Payment Rules:

  1. Pay on time – Late payments result in losing the winning bid and deposit.
  2. Verify payment processing – The county must confirm receipt before finalizing the sale.
  3. Cover additional costs – Expect recording fees and administrative expenses.
  4. Follow payment instructions – The Treasurer’s Office outlines specific steps to complete the purchase.
  5. Forfeiture rules – If buyers fail to pay, the property is re-listed in the next auction.
After the county receives full payment, the Treasurer’s Office issues a Treasurer’s Deed to the buyer. This process can take up to 30 days. The deed transfers ownership, but it does not guarantee a clear title.

Next Steps After Receiving the Deed:

  • Record the deed – File it with the Pend Oreille County Auditor’s Office to make ownership official.
  • Check for title issues – Some properties may have liens or legal claims that require legal action.
  • Confirm property boundaries – Hire a surveyor if needed to verify lot lines.
  • Handle all legal paperwork – Make sure all documents are in order for a smooth transfer.
  • Check for encroachments – Some properties may have structures crossing onto neighboring land.

What to Do After Winning a Property

New owners take full responsibility for the property immediately.

Next Steps for New Owners:

  1. Secure the property – Prevent trespassing or vandalism.
  2. Handle occupancy issues legally – If someone lives there, follow eviction laws.
  3. Assess the property condition – Some properties may need repairs or debris removal.
  4. Plan for future use – Decide whether to develop, rent, or sell the property.
  5. Stay current on taxes – Pay property taxes on time to avoid another foreclosure.
  6. Follow local regulations – Some properties may require permits for improvements.
  7. Inspect for hidden issues – Watch for problems like land erosion or flood risks.
